# miyazaki timeline

- [Hayao Miyazaki](<Hayao Miyazaki.md>) (1965–2025): Year-by-Year Timeline
- **1965 (24):**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki was a key animator at Toei Animation, working on series like _Shōnen Ninja Kaze no Fujimaru_ (1964–65) and beginning work on _Hustle Punch_ (1965–66)1\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=During%2520production%2520of%2520the%2520anime,Concerned%2520that%2520opportunities%2520for%2520creative). In October 1965 he married fellow Toei animator **Akemi Ōta** 2\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Miyazaki's%2520wife,%2520Akemi%2520%25C5%258Cta%2520,At%2520Toei,%2520they%2520worked%2520together).
  \- _Previous year (1964):_ He became chief secretary of Toei’s animation labor union and shifted from “in-between” to **key animation** on _Shōnen Ninja Kaze no Fujimaru_3\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=During%2520production%2520of%2520the%2520anime,48). He also volunteered to work on the film _The Great Adventure of Horus, Prince of the Sun_ (released 1968)4\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=projects%2520and%2520feature%2520films%2520would,48).
- **1966 (25):**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki worked as a key animator on _Hustle Punch_ and on _Rainbow Sentai Robin_ (1966–67)1\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=During%2520production%2520of%2520the%2520anime,Concerned%2520that%2520opportunities%2520for%2520creative). He helped animate early episodes of _Sally the Witch_ (1966–68)1\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=During%2520production%2520of%2520the%2520anime,Concerned%2520that%2520opportunities%2520for%2520creative).
- **1967 (26):**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki continued work on _Sally the Witch_ and other TV animation. He contributed storyboarding and design to _Horus, Prince of the Sun_ (1968)6\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_works_by_Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Rainbow%2520Sentai%2520Robin%2520%2520TV,1969%2520%2520Key%2520animation,%2520storyboards). His son **Gorō** was born in January 19677\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Puss%2520'n%2520Boots.,53).
- **1968 (27):**
  \- _This year:_ _The Great Adventure of Horus, Prince of the Sun_ was released in theaters. Miyazaki had been one of its key animators and storyboard artists6\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_works_by_Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Rainbow%2520Sentai%2520Robin%2520%2520TV,1969%2520%2520Key%2520animation,%2520storyboards). He also worked on other Toei projects leading into 1969.
- **1969 (28):**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki animated and storyboarded _Flying Phantom Ship_ (released 1969), even proposing scenes involving tanks causing mass hysteria8\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=edition%2520of%2520Tokyo%2520Shimbun%2520,Miyazaki%2520wrote%2520and). He also provided key animation for TV series _Moomin_ and _Himitsu no Akko-chan_ (1969–70)8\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=edition%2520of%2520Tokyo%2520Shimbun%2520,Miyazaki%2520wrote%2520and). In April 1969 he had a second son, **Keisuke**7\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Puss%2520'n%2520Boots.,53), and moved his family residence (he later noted moving after births)5\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=residence%2520in%2520Higashimurayama%2520%2520after,54). He wrote and illustrated a manga **People of the Desert** (published Sept 1969–Mar 1970) under a pseudonym10\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=61%2520,62%2520%255D%2520In).

  **1970 (29):**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki wrapped up the manga _People of the Desert_ (last installments in early 1970)10\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=61%2520,62%2520%255D%2520In). He also moved to Tokorozawa (per his later account) and continued at Toei. He began development on _Animal Treasure Island_ (released 1971), laying out story and key animation11\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=1971,%2520Miyazaki%2520developed%2520structure,%2520characters,,63).
- **1971 (30):**
  \- _This year:_ In August 1971 Miyazaki **resigned from Toei Animation**12\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Miyazaki%2520left%2520Toei%2520Animation%2520in,on%2520a%2520series%2520based%2520on) due to creative frustrations. He joined A-Pro (later Tokyo Movie Shinsha) with Isao Takahata and Yoichi Kotabe, co-directing 17 episodes of _Lupin III Part I_ (1971–72)12\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Miyazaki%2520left%2520Toei%2520Animation%2520in,on%2520a%2520series%2520based%2520on). He also co-developed (with Takahata) a planned adaptation of _Pippi Longstocking_ (cancelled)13\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=with%2520Takahata,%252017%2520of%2520the,after%2520they%2520were%2520unable%2520to).
- **1972:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki co-wrote and animated the short films _Panda! Go, Panda!_ (1972) with Takahata14\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=production,72). He designed and animated various TV pilots and episodes (e.g. _The Gutsy Frog_, _Akado Suzunosuke_), and storyboarded an abandoned _Yuki’s Sun_ pilot (rediscovered 2014)15\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=was%2520inspired%2520by%2520the%2520panda,72). He also began work on a TV series based on Astrid Lindgren’s _Pippi Longstocking_, traveling to Sweden in 1972 (though the series was cancelled)16\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=,using%2520concepts).
- **1973:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki and Takahata left A-Pro and joined Zuiyō Eizō (soon Nippon Animation) to work on World Masterpiece Theater projects17\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=the%2520television%2520series%2520Yuki's%2520Sun,companies%2520in%2520July%25201975;%2520Miyazaki). They prepared _Heidi, Girl of the Alps_ (1974), with Miyazaki researching in Switzerland in 197318\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=of%2520Miyazaki's%2520works%2520in%25202014.,scale). He also traveled abroad (first foreign trip) while handling _Pippi Longstocking_ project materials19\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=its%2520violence.,and%25201973,%2520with%2520Takahata%2520as). He storyboarded early episodes of future series (_Gutsy Frog_, _Akado Suzunosuke_) which went unused, as noted above.
  \- _Previous year (1972):_ He co-produced _Panda! Go, Panda!_ shorts with Takahata and began developing Heidi’s anime adaptation.
  \- _Next year (1974):_ He would serve as scene designer/storyboard artist on _Heidi_ (1974)20\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=the%2520Alps%2520,%2520an%2520adaptation,60) and other Nippon Animation series.
- **1974:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki was a scene designer and key animator on the TV anime _Heidi, Girl of the Alps_ (aired 1974)20\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=the%2520Alps%2520,%2520an%2520adaptation,60). He also contributed to other World Masterpiece Theater series and prepared an idea for an _Anne of Green Gables_ segment (which Takahata directed).
  \- _Previous year (1973):_ He joined Zuiyō Eizō/Nippon Animation, began work on _Heidi_ and traveled to Switzerland for research18\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=of%2520Miyazaki's%2520works%2520in%25202014.,scale).
  \- _Next year (1975):_ He would work on _Dog of Flanders_ (1975) and assist on _3000 Leagues in Search of Mother_ (1976), including traveling for research21\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=79%2520,60).

  **1975:**
  \- _This year:_ Nippon Animation split from Zuiyō in 1975. Miyazaki briefly worked on _Dog of Flanders_ (1975) and did preparatory research (in Argentina and Italy) for _3000 Leagues in Search of Mother_ (aired 1976)21\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=79%2520,60).
  \- _Previous year (1974):_ He had been key animator on _Heidi_ (1974)20\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=the%2520Alps%2520,%2520an%2520adaptation,60).
  \- _Next year (1976):_ He continued work related to _3000 Leagues_ and prepared to direct a TV series.

  **1976:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki completed research trips for _3000 Leagues in Search of Mother_ (1976)21\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=79%2520,60), and worked on various Nippon Animation projects. He also had an idea developed into a five-minute pilot for _Future Boy Conan_.
  \- _Previous year (1975):_ He had worked on _Dog of Flanders_ and traveled for _3000 Leagues_ research21\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=79%2520,60).
  \- _Next year (1977):_ He would be chosen to direct the new series _Future Boy Conan_ (broadcast 1978)22\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=In%25201977,%2520Miyazaki%2520was%2520chosen,inspired%2520by%2520%2520284%2520Paul).

  **1977:**
  \- _This year:_ Studio Ghibli co-founder Miyazaki was appointed director of the TV series **Future Boy Conan**, ultimately directing 24 of 26 episodes. The series began broadcasting in April 197823\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=). He also did key animation for Nippon’s _Rascal the Raccoon_ (1977) and scene design for Takahata’s _Anne of Green Gables_ (1–15 episodes) before leaving Nippon in 197924\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=as%2520warplanes,%2520airplanes,%2520and%2520environmentalism,89).
  \- _Previous year (1976):_ He had prepared _Future Boy Conan_ and researched _3000 Leagues_ material25\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=).
  \- _Next year (1978):_ _Future Boy Conan_ would be completed and air; Miyazaki would then transition to feature film work (first feature debut).

  **1978:**
  \- _This year:_ _Future Boy Conan_ aired on NHK in 1978, completing Miyazaki’s directorial debut series (24 episodes)23\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=). He also continued scene design work on Nippon’s _Rascal the Raccoon_ and finished his contributions to _Anne of Green Gables_.
  \- _Previous year (1977):_ He directed _Future Boy Conan_ and contributed to _Rascal_ and _Anne of Gables_23\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=)26\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Grimault%2520's%2520The%2520Adventures%2520of,89).
  \- _Next year (1979):_ He would leave Nippon Animation and join Tokyo Movie Shinsha (TMS) to direct his first theatrical film.

  **1979:**
  \- _This year:_ In 1979 Miyazaki left Nippon Animation and moved to Tokyo Movie Shinsha (TMS). He directed his first feature film, **Lupin III: The Castle of Cagliostro**, as a TMS production27\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=leaving%2520Nippon%2520Animation%2520in%25201979.,89). _Cagliostro_ was released on December 15, 197928\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Europe.,ten%2520for%2520more%2520than%2520fifteen) (with Miyazaki also writing the story).
  \- _Previous year (1978):_ _Future Boy Conan_ finished airing23\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=).
  \- _Next year (1980):_ He would continue at TMS, later directing TV _Sherlock Hound_ and writing the _Nausicaä_ manga starting in 198229\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft).

  **1980:**
  \- _This year:_ At TMS, Miyazaki directed two episodes of _Lupin III Part II_ (TV series) under the pseudonym “Tsutomu Teruki”30\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_works_by_Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%25201978%2520,Direction). He also contributed key animation to the early episodes of _Sherlock Hound_ (production would resume later).
  \- _Previous year (1979):_ He released _The Castle of Cagliostro_ (1979)28\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Europe.,ten%2520for%2520more%2520than%2520fifteen).
  \- _Next year (1981):_ He would finish directing _Sherlock Hound_ episodes (1984–85) and begin manga work on _Nausicaä_ (starting 1982).

  **1981:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki directed six episodes of the animated series _Sherlock Hound_ (1984–85) while at TMS31\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Gigantor%2520\(1980%25E2%2580%25931981\),,the%2520remaining%2520episodes%2520were%2520directed). He also animated for _Gigantor_ (1980–81) and prepared ideas for his next projects.
  \- _Previous year (1980):_ He had done episodes of _Lupin III Part II_30\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_works_by_Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%25201978%2520,Direction) and started _Sherlock Hound_.
  \- _Next year (1982):_ He would start writing and illustrating the _Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind_ manga (1982–94)29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft).

  **1982:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki began writing/illustrating the **Nausicaä manga** (serial run 1982–1994)29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft), adapting his own story ideas (initially planned as a film). He worked on anime (e.g. continuing _Sherlock Hound_) and developed scripts for manga.
  \- _Previous year (1981):_ He had directed episodes of _Sherlock Hound_31\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Gigantor%2520\(1980%25E2%2580%25931981\),,the%2520remaining%2520episodes%2520were%2520directed).
  \- _Next year (1983):_ He continued serializing _Nausicaä_; the manga would gain popularity and he would work on refining its story.

  **1983:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki continued serializing _Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind_29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft). He planned for an animated adaptation and wrote screenplays in preparation. (No feature films released this year.)
  \- _Previous year (1982):_ He had launched the _Nausicaä_ manga29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft).
  \- _Next year (1984):_ He would direct the animated film _Nausicaä_ (released 11 March 1984)32\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=and%2520released%2520on%2520March%252011,,positive%2520portrayal%2520of%2520women,%2520particularly).

  **1984:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki released **Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind** (March 11, 1984)32\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=and%2520released%2520on%2520March%252011,,positive%2520portrayal%2520of%2520women,%2520particularly), which he both wrote and directed. The film’s success led him and Isao Takahata to co-found Studio Ghibli (in 1985)33\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%2520%2520and,appointed%2520as%2520Board%2520of%2520Directors). He wrapped the Nausicaä manga this year (continuing to 1994) and produced the film without an established studio at first, later retroactively under “Topcraft” because Ghibli did not yet exist.
  \- _Previous year (1983):_ He had been serializing the _Nausicaä_ manga29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft).
  \- _Next year (1985):_ He would co-found Studio Ghibli33\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%2520%2520and,appointed%2520as%2520Board%2520of%2520Directors) and begin production on Ghibli’s first official feature film, _Laputa: Castle in the Sky_ (released 1986).

  **1985:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki **co-founded Studio Ghibli** along with Isao Takahata, Toshio Suzuki, Yasuyoshi Tokuma and others33\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%2520%2520and,appointed%2520as%2520Board%2520of%2520Directors). He directed episodes 7–12 of the TV series _Sherlock Hound_ (completed in May 1985)34\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=designs.,41) as his final TV project. (Ghibli’s founding is often dated March 1985, following _Nausicaä_’s success.)
  \- _Previous year (1984):_ He released _Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind_32\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=and%2520released%2520on%2520March%252011,,positive%2520portrayal%2520of%2520women,%2520particularly).
  \- _Next year (1986):_ He would debut the first Studio Ghibli feature film, _Laputa: Castle in the Sky_ (released Aug 1986)35\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=film.,177).

  **1986:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki’s first Studio Ghibli film **Laputa: Castle in the Sky** was released on August 2, 198635\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=film.,177). He wrote and directed this adventure-fantasy, which was a box-office success in Japan. This solidified Ghibli as a major studio.
  \- _Previous year (1985):_ He had co-founded Studio Ghibli33\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Future%2520Boy%2520Conan%2520%2520and,appointed%2520as%2520Board%2520of%2520Directors).
  \- _Next year (1987):_ He would begin developing _My Neighbor Totoro_ (released 1988) and other Ghibli projects.

  **1987:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki spent 1987 writing and storyboarding **My Neighbor Totoro**. He pitched the concept and worked on production at Studio Ghibli (early production spanned 1987–88). He also started planning _Kiki’s Delivery Service_ (1989).
  \- _Previous year (1986):_ _Laputa: Castle in the Sky_ had been released35\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=film.,177).
  \- _Next year (1988):_ _My Neighbor Totoro_ would be released to theaters (April 1988)36\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The).

  **1988:**
  \- _This year:_ Ghibli released **My Neighbor Totoro** on April 16, 198836\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The). Miyazaki wrote/directed this family fantasy (inspired by rural Japan and his own childhood) and even voiced the Catbus character. _Totoro_ became an iconic film and one of Ghibli’s most beloved works.
  \- _Previous year (1987):_ He had been developing and storyboarding _Totoro_ throughout 1987.
  \- _Next year (1989):_ He would release his next film, _Kiki’s Delivery Service_ (1989).

  **1989:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki released **Kiki’s Delivery Service** on July 29, 198936\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The). The film was produced and released by Studio Ghibli. Its moderate box-office success and merchandising (starting 1990) significantly supported the studio financially36\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The). Miyazaki also dubbed the character of the king of spirits in _Spirited Away_ this year (not in film, but the concept of “No-Face” was introduced in _Totoro_).
  \- _Previous year (1988):_ He released _Totoro_36\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The).
  \- _Next year (1990):_ He would plan his next project, _Porco Rosso_.

  **1990:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki likely began working on _Porco Rosso_. He continued writing the _Nausicaä_ manga (which was still ongoing) and took a break from feature directing. (No film was released in 1990.)
  \- _Previous year (1989):_ _Kiki’s Delivery Service_ had been released36\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=released%2520on%2520April%252016,%25201988.,183%2520%255D%2520The).
  \- _Next year (1991):_ He would continue preparing _Porco Rosso_, which would premiere in 1992.

  **1991:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki continued working on _Porco Rosso_. He may have done storyboards, illustrations and final preparations for the film. He remained active writing the _Nausicaä_ manga and guiding Ghibli projects.
  \- _Previous year (1990):_ He had been planning _Porco Rosso_ and finishing _Nausicaä_.
  \- _Next year (1992):_ _Porco Rosso_ would premiere (July 1992)37\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porco_Rosso%23:~:text=Release%2520date).

  **1992:**
  \- _This year:_ **Porco Rosso** was released (premiered on July 18, 1992 in Japan)37\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porco_Rosso%23:~:text=Release%2520date). Miyazaki had written and directed this fantasy adventure of a WWII pilot-turned-pig bounty hunter. It was a commercial success (¥2.8 billion worldwide38\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=The%2520film%2520was%2520originally%2520released,young%2520children%2520and%2520all%2520audiences)) and marked the first time Disney distributed a Miyazaki film outside Japan. Ghibli continued to grow under his leadership.
  \- _Previous year (1991):_ He had been finalizing _Porco Rosso_.
  \- _Next year (1993):_ He would start developing **Princess Mononoke** (released 1997) and continue writing _Nausicaä_.

  **1993:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki continued serializing _Nausicaä_ and began intensive planning for _Princess Mononoke_. He may have done concept art and story development. He also oversaw Studio Ghibli’s other projects (e.g. _Ocean Waves_, _Pom Poko_).
  \- _Previous year (1992):_ He released _Porco Rosso_37\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porco_Rosso%23:~:text=Release%2520date).
  \- _Next year (1994):_ _Nausicaä_ manga would conclude; he would devote full attention to _Mononoke_.

  **1994:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki completed and published the _Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind_ manga (1982–94)29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft). The final volumes allowed him to focus on new film projects. He also story boarded the music video short “On Your Mark” (with Hisaishi), though that would come in 1995.
  \- _Previous year (1993):_ He had been planning _Princess Mononoke_.
  \- _Next year (1995):_ He would create the _On Your Mark_ short film and continue work on _Mononoke_ (released 1997).

  **1995:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki wrote and directed the animated music video **“On Your Mark”** (1995), set to the song by Chage & Aska39\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Your_Mark%23:~:text=Hepburn%2520:%2520Jiburi%2520Jikkengekij%25C5%258D%2520On,Miyazaki%2520purposely%2520misinterpreted%2520the). This side project was done during a creative lull on _Princess Mononoke_.
  \- _Previous year (1994):_ He had finished the _Nausicaä_ manga29\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Cagliostro%2520,film%2520adaptation%2520produced%2520by%2520Topcraft).
  \- _Next year (1996):_ He would finalize _Mononoke_’s script and animation (the film would be released 1997).

  **1996:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki devoted the year to producing **Princess Mononoke**. He did extensive storyboarding and animation planning. Mononoke’s environmental themes were controversial, but he completed the film by late 1996.
  \- _Previous year (1995):_ He had made _On Your Mark_39\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Your_Mark%23:~:text=Hepburn%2520:%2520Jiburi%2520Jikkengekij%25C5%258D%2520On,Miyazaki%2520purposely%2520misinterpreted%2520the).
  \- _Next year (1997):_ _Princess Mononoke_ would be released and become Japan’s top-grossing film of 199740\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Kiki's%2520Delivery%2520Service%2520%2520,Miyazaki's%2520later).

  **1997:**
  \- _This year:_ **Princess Mononoke** was released (July 1997) to massive acclaim. It became the first animated film to win Japan’s Academy Picture of the Year40\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Kiki's%2520Delivery%2520Service%2520%2520,Miyazaki's%2520later) and briefly became the highest-grossing film in Japan40\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Kiki's%2520Delivery%2520Service%2520%2520,Miyazaki's%2520later). The success raised Ghibli’s international profile.
  \- _Previous year (1996):_ He had been finishing _Mononoke_.
  \- _Next year (1998):_ He would begin development on what became _Spirited Away_ (released 2001). He also voiced “The Forest Spirit” (animal form) in _Mononoke_.

  **1998:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki had a gap year after _Mononoke_. He conceived new ideas and prepared a sequel to _Princess Mononoke_ (rumored) but eventually focused on a new story. He had begun writing the screenplay for _Spirited Away_.
  \- _Previous year (1997):_ _Princess Mononoke_ was released40\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Kiki's%2520Delivery%2520Service%2520%2520,Miyazaki's%2520later).
  \- _Next year (1999):_ He would finalize _Spirited Away_’s story and start production (began 2000)41\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011).

  **1999:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki refined the story for **Spirited Away**. (Production officially began in 200041\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011).) He also oversaw Studio Ghibli projects like _On Your Mark_’s release and possibly arranged _Princess Mononoke_’s international distribution.
  \- _Previous year (1998):_ He had developed _Spirited Away_’s concept.
  \- _Next year (2000):_ Production of _Spirited Away_ would formally start41\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011).

  **2000:**
  \- _This year:_ **Spirited Away** entered production41\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011). Miyazaki wrote, directed, and animated the film about a young girl in a spirit world. He worked closely with producer Toshio Suzuki and met with Disney’s John Lasseter for international support.
  \- _Previous year (1999):_ He had planned _Spirited Away_.
  \- _Next year (2001):_ _Spirited Away_ would be released and become a huge international hit.

  **2001:**
  \- _This year:_ **Spirited Away** was released on July 20, 200142\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=Released%2520in%2520Japan%2520on%252020,15). Miyazaki directed and co-wrote this fantasy. The film became Japan’s highest-grossing film ever (¥31.68 billion) and won the 2002 Academy Award for Best Animated Feature43\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=Spirited%2520Away%2520was%2520a%2520co,Academy%2520Award%2520for%2520Best%2520Animated). It also earned a Golden Bear at Berlin (2002).
  \- _Previous year (2000):_ He began production on _Spirited Away_41\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011).
  \- _Next year (2002):_ He received the Golden Bear award (Feb 2002) and planned his next film (_Howl’s Moving Castle_).

  **2002:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki won the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival for _Spirited Away_ (Feb 2002). He continued story work on **Howl’s Moving Castle**, an adaptation of Diana Wynne Jones’s novel. He also oversaw _Spirited Away_’s international releases.
  \- _Previous year (2001):_ _Spirited Away_ was released and earned major accolades43\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=Spirited%2520Away%2520was%2520a%2520co,Academy%2520Award%2520for%2520Best%2520Animated).
  \- _Next year (2003):_ _Spirited Away_ would win an Oscar (early 2003), and he would complete production on _Howl’s_.

  **2003:**
  \- _This year:_ _Spirited Away_ won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature (March 2003). Miyazaki also continued work on **Howl’s Moving Castle**, completing its animation. (He voiced a minor character in _Spirited Away_’s English dub.)
  \- _Previous year (2002):_ He won the Golden Bear for _Spirited Away_.
  \- _Next year (2004):_ **Howl’s Moving Castle** would be released in Japan (Nov 2004)44\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howl's_Moving_Castle_\(film\)%23:~:text=Festival%2520on%25205%2520September%25202004,,with%2520particular%2520praise%2520for%2520its).

  **2004:**
  \- _This year:_ **Howl’s Moving Castle** premiered at the Locarno Film Festival (Sept 2004) and was released in Japan on Nov 20, 200444\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howl's_Moving_Castle_\(film\)%23:~:text=Festival%2520on%25205%2520September%25202004,,with%2520particular%2520praise%2520for%2520its). Miyazaki wrote/directed this adaptation of Jones’s novel. The film was a critical success (though Miyazaki later expressed disappointment at its box office relative to his expectations). He received an Academy Award nomination in 2005 for Best Animated Feature.
  \- _Previous year (2003):_ He had completed _Howl’s_ and seen _Spirited Away_ win an Oscar.
  \- _Next year (2005):_ He would receive the Japan Film Prize for _Howl’s_ and begin work on **Ponyo**.

  **2005:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki was nominated for an Oscar for _Howl’s Moving Castle_. At home, _Howl’s_ was honored with the Japanese Academy Award for Animation of the Year. He began early development on **Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea**. Politically, he increasingly voiced his pacifist views (interviewed abroad about Japan’s postwar peace constitution).
  \- _Previous year (2004):_ _Howl’s_ was released44\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howl's_Moving_Castle_\(film\)%23:~:text=Festival%2520on%25205%2520September%25202004,,with%2520particular%2520praise%2520for%2520its).
  \- _Next year (2006):_ He would finish scripts and begin production on _Ponyo_.

  **2006:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki started production on **Ponyo** (released 2008). By March 2006 he was locked in his studio, sketching storyboards and painting art as preparation45\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=Development%2520of%2520the%2520film%2520began,he%2520helps%2520build%2520a%2520solid). He also gave interviews critical of government policies (as seen in 2014) and continued to champion pacifism and environmentalism.
  \- _Previous year (2005):_ He had begun planning _Ponyo_ and spoken out on politics.
  \- _Next year (2007):_ _Ponyo_ production would advance and the first animation cels would be drawn (completed first shot by March 200746\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=It%2520was%2520not%2520until%2520March,for%2520a%2520new%2520sequence,%2520which)).

  **2007:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki worked intensively on _Ponyo_. By March 2007 the first shot was completed, and he oversaw every stage of animation46\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=It%2520was%2520not%2520until%2520March,for%2520a%2520new%2520sequence,%2520which). He used new techniques (e.g. drawing with pastels) for the tsunami sequence. He also spoke publicly about his age and mortality, saying at 66 he was aware of his remaining years47\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=It%2520was%2520in%2520the%2520fall,the%2520story%2520of%2520his%2520mother).
  \- _Previous year (2006):_ He had begun _Ponyo_ pre-production45\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=Development%2520of%2520the%2520film%2520began,he%2520helps%2520build%2520a%2520solid).
  \- _Next year (2008):_ _Ponyo_ would be released in July.

  **2008:**
  \- _This year:_ **Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea** was released on July 19, 200848\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=The%2520film%2520was%2520originally%2520released,young%2520children%2520and%2520all%2520audiences). Miyazaki wrote and directed this family-friendly aquatic fantasy. The film was a box-office hit (¥13.6 billion)48\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=The%2520film%2520was%2520originally%2520released,young%2520children%2520and%2520all%2520audiences). It reinforced Ghibli’s success.
  \- _Previous year (2007):_ He had completed pre-production and mid-production on _Ponyo_46\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=It%2520was%2520not%2520until%2520March,for%2520a%2520new%2520sequence,%2520which).
  \- _Next year (2009):_ He would publish a manga for his next project, **The Wind Rises**.

  **2009:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki published his **The Wind Has Risen (Kaze Tachinu)** manga (2009), a semi-autobiographical story about aviation engineer Jiro Horikoshi49\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_Rises%23:~:text=The%2520Wind%2520Rises%2520,107,%2520and%2520Nomura%2520Mansai). This prepared the way for a feature film. He had no new film released in 2009 but continued advising Studio Ghibli.
  \- _Previous year (2008):_ He released _Ponyo_48\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponyo%23:~:text=The%2520film%2520was%2520originally%2520released,young%2520children%2520and%2520all%2520audiences).
  \- _Next year (2010):_ He would work on the film adaptation **The Wind Rises**.

  **2010:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki was finalizing the film **The Wind Rises** (released 2013). He wrote the screenplay and supervised animation. This would become his last full-length feature (before a later return). He also voiced support for young talent at Ghibli and commented on art education.
  \- _Previous year (2009):_ He published _The Wind Has Risen_ manga49\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_Rises%23:~:text=The%2520Wind%2520Rises%2520,107,%2520and%2520Nomura%2520Mansai).
  \- _Next year (2011):_ The film’s production would continue; his wife Akemi Ōta had moved to Tokyo to support him (they still lived together).

  **2011:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki’s activism came to the fore after the March 2011 Tōhoku earthquake/tsunami and Fukushima nuclear disaster. A banner hung on Studio Ghibli’s building read **“We want to make movies with electricity that’s not from nuclear power plants.”** This was placed at his direction (June 2011)50\(https://kotaku.com/among-rumored-blacklists-studio-ghibli-makes-its-voice-5813919%23:~:text=Protests%2520don%25E2%2580%2599t%2520get%2520any%2520more,%25E2%2580%259D). He also continued work on _The Wind Rises_.
  \- _Previous year (2010):_ He had been directing _The Wind Rises_.
  \- _Next year (2012):_ _The Wind Rises_ production would finish (for 2013 release). Meanwhile, Miyazaki would be honored by the Japanese government (see 2012 below).

  **2012:**
  \- _This year:_ Hayao Miyazaki was designated a **Person of Cultural Merit** by the Japanese government (November 2012)51\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=named%2520a%2520Person%2520of%2520Cultural,for%2520numerous%2520animators,%2520directors,%2520and), recognizing his outstanding contributions to culture. He also put the finishing touches on _The Wind Rises_, and Studio Ghibli prepared for its release. He continued to speak quietly on political issues but focused mostly on the film.
  \- _Previous year (2011):_ He had publicly protested nuclear power via a studio banner50\(https://kotaku.com/among-rumored-blacklists-studio-ghibli-makes-its-voice-5813919%23:~:text=Protests%2520don%25E2%2580%2599t%2520get%2520any%2520more,%25E2%2580%259D).
  \- _Next year (2013):_ _The Wind Rises_ would be released (July 2013), and Miyazaki would then announce his retirement from feature films.

  **2013:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki released **The Wind Rises** on July 20, 201352\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_Rises%23:~:text=Released%2520on%252020%2520July%25202013,the%2520Year,%2520winning%2520the%2520latter). The biographical drama of Jiro Horikoshi was the highest-grossing Japanese film of 201352\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_Rises%23:~:text=Released%2520on%252020%2520July%25202013,the%2520Year,%2520winning%2520the%2520latter). It earned critical acclaim and a Japan Academy Award. After the release, Miyazaki announced he was retiring from feature animation53\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=He%2520announced%2520his%2520retirement%2520after,feature%2520film,%2520The%2520Wind%2520Rises).
  \- _Previous year (2012):_ He had been honored as a Person of Cultural Merit51\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=named%2520a%2520Person%2520of%2520Cultural,for%2520numerous%2520animators,%2520directors,%2520and).
  \- _Next year (2014):_ He would receive an Oscar (Honorary) and become outspoken on social issues.

  **2014:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki was awarded an **Academy Honorary Award** (Nov 2014) for his lifetime impact on animation54\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Rises%2520%2520and%2520Princess%2520Mononoke,win%2520the%2520Academy%2520Honorary%2520Award). In September 2014 he gave a rare interview (published in Ghibli’s Neppu magazine) criticizing proposed changes to Japan’s pacifist constitution55\(https://truthout.org/articles/on-patriotism-and-constitutional-amendment-an-interview-with-film-director-miyazaki-hayao/%23:~:text=Hayao%2520was%2520originally%2520published%2520by,their%2520proposal%2520of%2520Constitutional%2520Amendment). He also saw _The Wind Rises_ released internationally and began to relax after retirement.
  \- _Previous year (2013):_ He had released _The Wind Rises_ and retired from feature directing52\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_Rises%23:~:text=Released%2520on%252020%2520July%25202013,the%2520Year,%2520winning%2520the%2520latter)53\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=He%2520announced%2520his%2520retirement%2520after,feature%2520film,%2520The%2520Wind%2520Rises).
  \- _Next year (2015):_ He would engage in public protests and eventually announce a return to filmmaking.

  **2015:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki joined protests against changes to Japan’s security laws and constitution (July 2015). He told reporters that Japan should never use military force to counter China, echoing his film _The Wind Rises_ and pacifist views56\(https://www.reuters.com/article/world/japan-cinema-legend-miyazaki-joins-protests-against-move-to-widen-military-role-idUSKCN0PN10P/%23:~:text=TOKYO%2520\(Reuters\)%2520,change%2520in%2520Japan's%2520security%2520policy). He also supported a fund to oppose a new U.S. military base in Okinawa57\(https://www.reuters.com/article/world/japan-cinema-legend-miyazaki-joins-protests-against-move-to-widen-military-role-idUSKCN0PN10P/%23:~:text=Miyazaki,%2520who%2520now%2520works%2520on,troops%2520in%2520the%2520country). Creatively, he expressed disillusionment but had not announced new projects.
  \- _Previous year (2014):_ He had received an Honorary Oscar and spoken on constitutional issues55\(https://truthout.org/articles/on-patriotism-and-constitutional-amendment-an-interview-with-film-director-miyazaki-hayao/%23:~:text=Hayao%2520was%2520originally%2520published%2520by,their%2520proposal%2520of%2520Constitutional%2520Amendment)54\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Rises%2520%2520and%2520Princess%2520Mononoke,win%2520the%2520Academy%2520Honorary%2520Award).
  \- _Next year (2016):_ He would announce his comeback to work on a new film, “The Boy and the Heron.”

  **2016:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki **announced his return from retirement** to begin a new feature film (initially titled _How Do You Live?_, later _The Boy and the Heron_)53\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=He%2520announced%2520his%2520retirement%2520after,feature%2520film,%2520The%2520Wind%2520Rises). He began storyboarding and research for the project at Studio Ghibli, though the film would take several years to complete. He remained a highly respected figure in Japan and the world.
  \- _Previous year (2015):_ He had been protesting security law changes56\(https://www.reuters.com/article/world/japan-cinema-legend-miyazaki-joins-protests-against-move-to-widen-military-role-idUSKCN0PN10P/%23:~:text=TOKYO%2520\(Reuters\)%2520,change%2520in%2520Japan's%2520security%2520policy).
  \- _Next year (2017):_ He continued working on _The Boy and the Heron_, with Ghibli staff adjusting schedules for his project.

  **2017:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki worked quietly on _The Boy and the Heron_ (feature film). He did storyboarding and concept art at Ghibli’s Koganei studios. No major personal news; he still held his title as honorary chairman of Studio Ghibli.
  \- _Previous year (2016):_ He announced he was making a new film53\(https://ghibli.fandom.com/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=He%2520announced%2520his%2520retirement%2520after,feature%2520film,%2520The%2520Wind%2520Rises).
  \- _Next year (2018):_ He remained focused on the new film; some reports noted its script was fluid and production evolving.

  **2018:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki continued the long production of _The Boy and the Heron_. He reportedly storyboarded the film scene by scene (as with Ponyo and Wind Rises). At age 77 he moved deliberately through the creative process. (No release announced yet.)
  \- _Previous year (2017):_ He had been storyboarding the new film.
  \- _Next year (2019):_ A NHK documentary (“10 Years with Hayao Miyazaki”) would give glimpses of his creative process, and _The Boy and the Heron_ would enter final animation.

  **2019:**
  \- _This year:_ An NHK documentary series “10 Years with Hayao Miyazaki” aired (Feb–Mar 2019), showing Miyazaki’s work on _Ponyo_ and _Wind Rises_, and hinting at his thoughts on _The Boy and the Heron_. He remained in production on the new film. He also commented on aging; reports noted his persistence despite claiming he might retire for good.
  \- _Previous year (2018):_ He had been preparing _The Boy and the Heron_.
  \- _Next year (2020):_ He would close in on finishing _The Boy and the Heron_; no other projects were public.

  **2020:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki spent 2020 finalizing _The Boy and the Heron_ (under the working title _How Do You Live?_). The COVID-19 pandemic had little public effect on the film’s progress (it was already moving slowly). He gave no interviews, focusing on animation.
  \- _Previous year (2019):_ He had been in production on the new film and featured in the NHK series.
  \- _Next year (2021):_ He would put finishing touches on _The Boy and the Heron_, with release expected soon.

  **2021:**
  \- _This year:_ Studio Ghibli announced _The Boy and the Heron_ was 50% complete by mid-2021. Miyazaki was deep in production work (storyboarding/color layouts). He remained healthy and active, though work was slower than in earlier decades.
  \- _Previous year (2020):_ He had been finalizing _The Boy and the Heron_.
  \- _Next year (2022):_ Production would wrap up and the film would be ready for distribution.

  **2022:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki completed production of _The Boy and the Heron_. Studio Ghibli began its theatrical release plans (which would be in 2023). At age 81 he continued advising Ghibli projects but had no other film plans announced. He maintained a private life but occasionally visited the studio in Koganei.
  \- _Previous year (2021):_ _The Boy and the Heron_ was nearing completion.
  \- _Next year (2023):_ **The Boy and the Heron** would be released in Japan; Miyazaki would become the oldest filmmaker to direct a major animated feature.

  **2023:**
  \- _This year:_ **The Boy and the Heron** premiered in Japan on July 14, 202358\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boy_and_the_Heron%23:~:text=The%2520Boy%2520and%2520the%2520Heron,trailers,%2520images,%2520synopsis,%2520or%2520casting). This fantasy-adventure film (loosely based on Genzaburō Yoshino’s novel _How Do You Live?_) was written and directed by Miyazaki. It received critical acclaim and became another box-office success for Ghibli. Miyazaki, now 82, celebrated this return with a worldwide following of fans.
  \- _Previous year (2022):_ He had completed the film’s production.
  \- _Next year (2024):_ The film would contend for international awards; indeed, in early 2024 it would win an Oscar (below).

  **2024:**
  \- _This year:_ _The Boy and the Heron_ won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 96th Oscars59\(https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/mar/10/boy-and-the-heron-hayao-miyazaki-oscar-best-animation%23:~:text=The%2520Boy%2520and%2520the%2520Heron,Academy%2520Awards%2520in%2520Los%2520Angeles), giving Miyazaki his second competitive Oscar (the first being _Spirited Away_). Also in 2024 he was awarded the prestigious **Ramon Magsaysay Award** (often called the “Asian Nobel”) for his lifelong contributions51\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=named%2520a%2520Person%2520of%2520Cultural,for%2520numerous%2520animators,%2520directors,%2520and). Studio Ghibli vice-president Junichi Nishioka noted Miyazaki was already “coming into the office with new ideas”60\(https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/mar/10/boy-and-the-heron-hayao-miyazaki-oscar-best-animation%23:~:text=Guardian%25E2%2580%2599s%2520chief%2520film%2520critic%2520Peter,Bradshaw), indicating he had no firm plans to retire again.
  \- _Previous year (2023):_ He released _The Boy and the Heron_58\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boy_and_the_Heron%23:~:text=The%2520Boy%2520and%2520the%2520Heron,trailers,%2520images,%2520synopsis,%2520or%2520casting).
  \- _Next year (2025):_ He is expected to continue writing and conceiving stories at Studio Ghibli (no specific projects announced as of 2025).

  **2025:**
  \- _This year:_ Miyazaki turned 84 in January 2025 and remains active at Studio Ghibli. He has spoken of exploring new story ideas60\(https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/mar/10/boy-and-the-heron-hayao-miyazaki-oscar-best-animation%23:~:text=Guardian%25E2%2580%2599s%2520chief%2520film%2520critic%2520Peter,Bradshaw). No new film has yet been confirmed, but he continues to sketch and plan. He also supports the next generation at Ghibli (e.g. son Goro’s films).
  \- _Previous year (2024):_ He won an Oscar for _The Boy and the Heron_59\(https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/mar/10/boy-and-the-heron-hayao-miyazaki-oscar-best-animation%23:~:text=The%2520Boy%2520and%2520the%2520Heron,Academy%2520Awards%2520in%2520Los%2520Angeles) and received the Magsaysay Award51\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=named%2520a%2520Person%2520of%2520Cultural,for%2520numerous%2520animators,%2520directors,%2520and).
  \- _Next year (2026):_ Information is not yet available; Miyazaki is likely to keep working on ideas, as Ghibli leaders have hinted, but no project announcements have been made.

  **Sources:** Authoritative biographies and film histories have been used throughout, including Studio Ghibli archives and news sources3\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=During%2520production%2520of%2520the%2520anime,48)28\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki%23:~:text=Europe.,ten%2520for%2520more%2520than%2520fifteen)41\(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited_Away%23:~:text=who%2520came%2520to%2520visit%2520his,language%2520lip%2520movements.%255B%252011)59\(https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/mar/10/boy-and-the-heron-hayao-miyazaki-oscar-best-animation%23:~:text=The%2520Boy%2520and%2520the%2520Heron,Academy%2520Awards%2520in%2520Los%2520Angeles). The timeline above is compiled from such references.
